subject: Urgent: Post-deploy degradation — quantized model v2.1.0 causing latency & errors
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@velvetpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus@velvetpay.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Immediate: production degradation after model upgrade

Hi Rishi —

We pushed the Redwood-served model upgrade (model-2.1.0, quant profile: q4_0) at 13:00 PT today per the rollout plan. Since then we’ve observed a ~3x P99 latency increase for the payments NLP endpoint and a spike in 500/timeout errors. Accuracy checks on our regression set also show an uplift in incorrect entity extractions (~6% higher false positives).

This is impacting our evening batch and transaction monitoring alerts are firing. Our ops lead Marcus is on the thread. Can you escalate and advise immediate mitigations? We need either a quick rollback or traffic split to the prior model.

Sincerely,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Engineering — VelvetPay

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -08:00
Subject: FW: Immediate: production degradation after model upgrade

Team —

Picking up triage. Quick notes from infra and perf sampling:
- Deployed artifact: model-2.1.0 (intended quantization: q4_0).
- Observed behavior: token-level CPU spike on batch aggregator leading to longer scheduling latency, and several OOM-rescue retries on a subset of hosts (region-us-west-2).
- Repro locally with synthetic traces: p99 increases when sequence lengths > 256 and batch size auto-batching enabled.

Suggested mitigation steps (in order):
1) Start a canary rollback to model-2.0.7 for 20% of traffic to validate restoration.
2) Temporarily disable continuous batching for VelvetPay route (lowers throughput but cuts tail latency).
3) If rollback is clean, expand rollback to 100% and keep q4_0 disabled for now.

Attaching perf logs and a dashboard snapshot. Assigning to Neha to run quant-profile diff and Stephanie to create incident doc and customer-facing timeline.

[attachment: perf_logs_1119.zip]

—Monica
Monica Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Immediate: production degradation after model upgrade

Quick findings from quant-profile diff:
- The q4_0 profile used in v2.1.0 introduced a tighter packing scheme that reduces memory but changes some activation scaling heuristics; this appears to alter the kernel selection path under certain attention window sizes.
- Edge case: for sequences with many short sub-tokens (payments tokens + routing ids) the quantized kernels force a re-compute that interacts poorly with our batching heuristic and causes scheduler thrash.

Actionable: I can produce a patched quant profile (q4_0-vp-patch) that restores the previous kernel selection behavior while preserving most of the memory benefits. However patching will take ~3-4 hours to validate.

Recommendation for immediate customer mitigation: rollback to v2.0.7 (previous profile q4_0-legacy) and optionally plan a staged re-deploy with q4_0-vp-patch after validation.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Applied ML / Model Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@velvetpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus@velvetpay.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: production degradation after model upgrade

Elaine / Marcus —

Thanks for flagging this. We rolled back VelvetPay’s production route to model-2.0.7 at 08:20 PT and disabled continuous auto-batching for the route as a precaution. Early metrics show P99 latency returning to baseline and error rate back within your SLO. We’ve attached an incident summary and a dashboard snapshot for your review.

Next steps (planned):
- Redwood will run a validated staged re-deploy using the patched quant profile (q4_0-vp-patch) in our staging cluster and then a small canary (5%) with active monitoring. Target ETA to start the canary: 48 hours.
- We’ll share a post-incident report and a compensatory service credit for the impacted window (details via your account manager).

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll keep you closely updated. If you want an exec sync, I can get our Head of Product on a call this afternoon.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
